text: Third alarm. Here we go again.
Saturday. I don't want to go anywhere... but the return deadline is today.
Oh, it's the neighbor. Should I pretend I didn't see her?
I think we made eye contact... it's way too early to say hi.
...Nobody out there. Now's my chance.
Someone's in the hallway. Let's wait a little longer.
Please let no one get on. Please.
...Just watch the floor numbers. Only the floor numbers.
Stairs are better. My legs may ache, but my mind is at ease.
The management office. Head down, keep walking.
So many people. Maybe I'll put my earphones in.
The subway's faster... but I'd have to walk into that crowd.
The alley's longer but quiet. A little detour is fine.
The flyer guy. If I look at my phone, maybe I can slip past.
Thirty meters to my desk. Just make it past the pantry.
Laughter from the pantry. I'll get water later.
The team lead is looking this way. Focus on the monitor.
One comment in the meeting. I've rehearsed it a hundred times in my head.
I said it. My voice might have shaken, but I said it.
A restroom stall. Nobody calls my name in here.
Knock knock. ...Oh, I guess I've been in here a while.
Tofu, eggs, scallions. Stick to the list and be quick.
The sample stand. Make eye contact and it's over.
That person... where have I seen them? Oh, same class in high school.
I can't remember their name. Please don't remember me.
The staffed lane is short, but they'll chat. Self-checkout... look at that line.
The clerk's already looking. Three seconds of eye contact and she'll come over.
The fitting room. Let me catch my breath.
Team dinner. I just need to slip out before round two.
I need to pick a seat. A corner, near the door.
Nobody talks to the person grilling. Hard at work here.
My turn for the toast is coming. Breathe.
Everyone's busy planning round two. Time to quietly head out.
I can see home. Almost there.
Click. ...Now no one can come in.
I'm getting tired. Everything sounds louder than usual.
Was this hallway always this long?
My ears are ringing. I'm really at my limit.
My face is burning. It feels like everyone's staring at it.
My head is throbbing. I want to close my eyes for a moment.
The words are tangling. My thoughts are clear, but my mouth won't keep up.
My palms are sweaty. My phone might slip.
Why did I say it like that. Why. Why.
A call. My heart just dropped.
Unread notifications are piling up. Later. Later.
There's my person. Next to them, I don't have to talk.
I like that you never ask me anything.
Nothing but bills in the mailbox.
Let me sit a moment and just listen to the leaves.
It's still busy out there, but from here it looks quiet.
That answer was weird, right? It was definitely weird.
Thank you, friend. Really, thank you.
The plans got canceled. ...Honestly, I'm a little happy.
The doorbell. Even at home.
I didn't read the messages, so the team lead came in person.
I'm late. Everyone's going to look up when I walk in.
'Please keep noise down between floors.' ...That's not my keyboard, right? I wore headphones.
Too many options. The usual. Iced americano. Don't even pretend to think about it.
'Dogs must be leashed.' Nothing about cats. Bori doesn't go on walks anyway.
'Sign up for the company bowling tournament.' No reply counts as yes... clicking 'decline' right now.
Leftovers from the last meeting: 'Ways to boost communication.' Where do I go once it's boosted?
'Make your weekend more vibrant!' Skip the vibrant. Does anyone sell quiet weekends?
This week's calendar. The more blank squares, the calmer I feel. Saturday says 'return'.
'Buy one, get one free, today only.' Two means one less trip next week. Good deal.
Lucky mannequins. No one talks to them. ...Oh wait, the clerk is fixing their clothes too.
Bottom of the menu: 'Rice, 1,000 won.' Tonight my job is grilling meat and eating rice.
I like cafés. Once I get past 'For here?'
The convenience store. You can buy things without talking. I can breathe a little here.
The park. The wind covers up the voices a little.
The smell of home. Bori walks up, tail held high.
No one by the mailboxes. Today's a lucky day.
'Stay healthy through the change of seasons.' Everyone on the poster is beaming. I'd like to look that healthy.
'Unattended laundry will be moved to the bin.' Better not wander off while I wait.
A handwritten card by the register: 'Good books for quiet reading.' I think the owner gets me.
I only crossed one big street, and the noise dropped by half.
The pharmacy. The hardest part is saying my symptoms out loud.
The hum of washing machines. Strangely soothing.
A bookstore. Here, not talking is good manners.
A kid is waving. Wave back and it's over quickly.
The delivery guy. I just need to sign. Just sign.
'Just one minute' is never one minute. I know from experience.
Wednesday. Afternoon off. Just get through the morning and the rest is mine.
A box with my name on it. One signature and done. As long as he doesn't ask 'Nice weather, huh?'
A flea market. Browsing is nice, but 'Take a look!' is coming from every side.
12:40. Walking out the office door is the lightest moment of my week.
Rain outside. No umbrella. I'll stop by the convenience store.
My shoulders are getting soaked. Damp clothes cling to my skin.
Maintenance notice. Lucky I'm on the third floor. On the stairs I might not meet anyone.
Movers. The hallway's narrow. I'll hug the wall and squeeze by.
No need to time my hello in the hallway today.
The song's nice... but everyone's standing right there.
The traffic is quiet. On days like this, walking is nice.
The drilling echoes inside my skull. Maybe I'll take the alley.
A green vest. A hand holding flyers, pointed my way.
Is that... someone from my old job? They haven't seen me yet.
Our eyes met. Too late to pretend now.
A puppy. I love puppies, but talking with their owners...
Lots of empty seats. I get to pick a corner today.
The sky looks gloomy.
Eyes barely open and I'm already counting today's conversations.
Bori is meowing at my feet. Breakfast for her first.
It's dangerous outside the blanket. Still, I have to go.
People, people, people. I check my earphones.
Long wait at the crosswalk. The person next to me is on a call.
The alley is longer but quiet. I choose quiet.
Laughter from the pantry. The coffee can wait.
Take the flyer and a conversation starts. Don't take it... that's a conversation too.
The neighbor's shopping bags look heavy. Maybe I'll at least say hi.
Inside the stall. No one can see my face in here.
Why am I running? Out of breath, and now my mind's rushing too.
I'm not even late, but my feet keep speeding up.
Slow down. Running only makes it worse.
I let a work message slide. It'll only feel heavier later.
Tomorrow-me will handle it. ...Tomorrow-me is still me.
The team chat feels quieter lately. Probably just my imagination.
Skipped the management office's call again. There might be a notice on my door.
The longer I put off home stuff, the less homey home feels.
The package... if I don't get it today, the fridge goes empty.
Put off the groceries. Cup noodles for dinner again.
I put off replying. The guilt is slowly piling up.
I'll reply later. Later.
One more dodge and... they'll probably come find me in person.
Presentation day. Maybe practice once at the mirror.
"Hello, from Planning…" The me in the mirror looks better than expected.
It's over. I don't remember a word I said. But it's over.
If yesterday's presentation comes up… I'll just grill the meat.
Thump, thump. Upstairs is moving something again. At this hour.
That person… 402? The source of the thumping.
'Could you keep it a little quieter at night? :) — 302' Drew a smiley too. I'll hang it on their doorknob.
Memo pad by the door. Cat food, tissues, and 'breathe'.
Jiu is moving. Not far, Jiu said. Not far.
A nod. Done. The perfect conversation.
That's Seoyun. The only person at this company who never starts a conversation with me.
The container is still warm. …Did I even say thank you?
It's the neighbor. She'll ask about the braised beef. Just say it was good.
Loan desk. Can't help double-checking that nothing's overdue.
'Phones on silent in the reading room.' My favorite rule in the world.
Haircut, 18,000 won. 'How would you like it?' costs more than that.
Not today. Not brave enough yet to say 'whatever you think is best.'
'Feline combo vaccine, yearly.' Bori's next shot is… next month.
Haeoreum Stream. Two ducks floating side by side, saying nothing. Jealous.
'Today's class: breathing in silence.' If it's that kind of class…
Quiet. So quiet I can hear myself breathe. Nice.
The sound of water. The sound of no one talking to me.
Hair dryers. And soon, 'How would you like it?'
A dog in the waiting room is looking at me. The dog is fine. The owner is the issue.
The smell of mats. Is this a place where I don't have to talk?
The display says 'No. 7 arriving soon.' How soon is soon?
Window seat by the back door. Just look outside.
Rush-hour bus. Someone's bag is pressing into my back. Just three stops.
Should I say hi? Too late now. Keep looking out the window.
ATM. Machines don't ask 'What can we help you with?' Good machine.
Ticket 113. Seven people waiting. Just stare at the phone until my number's called.
Salt bread, cream buns, red bean buns. Choosing is nice, but 'Want it wrapped?' is waiting.
Tteokbokki, sundae, gimbap. The best item on the menu is the wall-facing seat.
The ticket machine's chime, low music. The bank is quiet but somehow tense.
Fresh-baked smell. Maybe I can stay here a moment.
"Welcome~" A place where no one cares if you come alone.
Smell of soil and flowers. The owner seems to be a person of few words.
An elderly person is looking around. I have a feeling they'll ask me the way.
A festival. It's pretty. And way too many people.
Something's on TV, but it's quiet. Good.
[Notice] Don't put food waste in with the bag. (3rd notice) …Third.
[Notice] Noise prevention: no heavy heel-walking after 10 p.m. Someone penciled '402, take note' and erased it.
[Notice] Elevator inspection. 'Sorry for the inconvenience' is in a different font every time.
[Notice] Redevelopment briefing next month. Someone wrote 'again?' underneath.
[Notice] Recycling day changed: Fri → Sat. This notice alone has changed four times.
[Notice] Lantern festival at the stream, 6 p.m. The management office staffer is listed as 'event crew'.
[Company notice] Kickoff for new project 'Chaeum', an office-supply subscription app. Still feels like someone else's problem.
[Company notice] New coffee machine in the break room. The sign says 'Keep talks short, keep coffee long.' I like it.
[Company notice] Request half-days and leave via messenger in advance. Did that today. Good job, me.
[Company notice] 10 a.m., meeting room: 'Chaeum' presentation. My name is in the presenter box. It's real.
[Company notice] Team dinner today at the barbecue place. Second round: TBD. TBD is the scariest part.
Ad: '18 minutes to Central Station.' Meaning 18 minutes pressed against strangers.
Ad: Muhan Corp. 'Chaeum' — we'll fill what your office needs. A company ad on my commute.
Ad: Haeoreum Stream lantern festival, this Saturday. Maybe I'll float one lantern.
Ad: Hanbit City reading week. Library reading room open till 10 p.m. Just knowing that is comforting.
TV: 'Hanbit City installs night lighting along Haeoreum Stream.' The owner switches to a drama rerun.
TV: 'Single-person households pass 30%.' That's why the snack bar's single seats are always full.
TV: Weather. Saturday, clear. Festival weather.
TV: 'Office subscription services heat up.' …Is that about Chaeum?
TV: 'Team-dinner culture shifts… more people heading home instead of a second round.' Let tonight be one of those.
TV: Live festival coverage. Just looking at the crowd on screen is tiring.
[Book of the month] 'The Uses of Time Alone'. Checked out. Someone like me borrowed it.
[Recruiting] Saturday 'Quiet Reading Club'. No talking required. …This exists?
[Notice] The reading room stays quiet even on festival day. Kindest sentence I've read today.
Quiet. No one here. Bori looks up. "You're back?"
Wind. I'm too fast for anyone to start a conversation. Nice.
